title: Campus-half floor hardcodes literal 10 while the total ask is derived — a future multiplier/volume re-tune silently drifts the campus pin
evidence:
EXPECTED := i64(stream_entries) * i64(surge.multiplier) * i64(WINDOW) // 2×1×10×WINDOW = 20×WINDOW
	testing.expectf(t, campus_window_spawns >= 10*WINDOW*95/100,
		"the campus half must land: in-window campus spawns %d < %d (10/tick × WINDOW × 0.95)", campus_window_spawns, 10*WINDOW*95/100)
detail: EXPECTED derives (campus+host streaming volumes × surge.multiplier × WINDOW), but the campus floor hardcodes the literal 10 (= campus volume 1 × multiplier 10). A multiplier or campus-volume re-tune silently mis-scales this pin, defeating the fold's derive-everything intent.
recommended_fix: Derive the campus floor from the catalog: sum streaming-entry volumes where source_role == .Campus, then × surge.multiplier × WINDOW × 95/100, mirroring the EXPECTED derivation.

title: fold-check prints the new tick-1 but never asserts it against the blessed manifest — a wrong current golden still PASSes
detail: The docstring claims new_tick1 is 'cross-checked against the blessed manifest', but the code only prints it; PASS/FAIL is set solely by the splice equality. A current golden blessed with a wrong tick-1 would still PASS.
recommended_fix: Read the current boot.t1 tick-1 (or take it as an arg) and assert new_tick1 equals it before returning PASS, making the cross-check mechanical.
